simple.meaning: לָחַךְ (lâchak) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to lick.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 6 times across Numbers, 1 Kings, Psalms, Isaiah, Micah, beginning at Numbers 22:4. Its contexts include family, offering, kingship, wilderness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לָחַךְ (H3897).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: לָחַךְ (lâchak) / H3897 is traced through Numbers 22:4, 1 Kings 18:38, Psalms 72:9, Isaiah 49:23 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Moab said to the elders of Midian, “Now this multitude will lick up all that is around us, as the ox licks up the grass of the field.”

definitions.full: H3897. lachak לחַךְ verb lick (Late Hebrew id. ; so Aramaic לְחַךְ ; Arabic ; - Qal Infinitive construct כִּלְחֹךְ Num 22:4 (E), followed by accusative; of ox licking up grass. Pi`el Perfect 3feminine singular לִחֵ֑כָה 1Kin 18:38 ; Imperfect 3masculine plural יְלַחֲכוּ Num 22:4 ; Micah 7:17 ; יְלַחֵ֑כוּ Psa 72:9 ; Isa 43:23 ; lick up (followed by accusative), fire from heaven the water in trench 1Kin 18:38 ; of Israel consuming produce of land Num 22:3 (E); especially ׳ל עָפָר lick the dust , sign of humiliation Micah 7:17 ; Psa 72:9 ; Isa 49:23 .
